quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What traffic light means you must stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe?
questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When you must stop at an intersection but see no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?

options.text: You do not need to stop.
Slow down to check if traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see at least 200 feet on both sides, even if you enter the other roadway.
Stop where you can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the other roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the other roadway.
questions.explanation: Stop at the point closest to the other roadway where you can see approaching traffic. Do not enter the other roadway to get a better view.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
questions.explanation: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, you can pass only if you are in the lane with the broken line.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A community group is picking up trash on the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road ahead in a work zone.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road ahead in a work zone.
questions.explanation: This sign alerts you that workers may be on or near the roadway ahead. Drive carefully through this area.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, what should you do?

options.text: Enter faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the speed of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic. Signal, find an opening, speed up, then merge into traffic smoothly.

questions.question: What does NOT affect how far a vehicle needs to stop?

options.text: Your vehicle's tire condition and type.

questions.correctAnswerText: The time of day.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition, road condition, and speed. The time of day does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line. What do you know right away?

options.text: Traffic moves in one direction only.
You must stay to the left of the broken lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in both directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken line means you can pass when it is safe.

questions.question: If an oncoming vehicle has its high beams on, where should you look?

options.text: The right side of the road.
The left side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded by the headlights. This lets you see well enough to stay in your lane until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: When you adjust your rearview mirror, what should you be able to see?

options.text: The passengers in the back seat.
Most of the lane next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The entire rear window.
questions.explanation: Adjust your rearview mirror so you can see the entire rear window. You should only have to move your eyes, not your head, to use this mirror.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is coming.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you of a steep hill, so adjust your speed to drive safely.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You can turn right or left.
Traffic only moves in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic only moves in the direction shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: A one-way sign tells you that traffic only moves in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: When parking uphill by a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires pointing straight.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking facing uphill by a curb, turn your steering wheel away from the curb. If your vehicle rolls, it will roll toward the curb and stop.

questions.question: A leaky exhaust system is dangerous because it can cause:
questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes harmful fumes from your vehicle. A leak allows carbon monoxide to enter the passenger area. Fix any leaks in your exhaust system right away.

questions.question: ____ of crashes happen within 25 miles of home.
questions.correctAnswerText: 75 percent
questions.explanation: 75 percent of crashes occur within 25 miles of home. Always wear your seat belt before you leave your driveway, even for short trips.

questions.question: When you are following other cars across railroad tracks with no signals or gates:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You can pass slower cars while crossing the tracks.
Make sure your car can cross completely without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your car can cross completely without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before driving onto railroad tracks, check that you have enough space to cross completely without stopping. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing any tracks.

questions.question: Red pavement markings or reflectors mean:
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter this road.
questions.explanation: Red pavement markings or reflectors mean you must not enter that road. If you see red reflectors or markings, do not go that way.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect how far it takes to stop your vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change based on your speed and road conditions.

questions.question: You are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. You should:

options.text: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot. Always check your mirrors and use your turn signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads:

options.text: Always drive at the maximum speed limit.
Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, avoid sudden changes in speed or direction. Slow down and do not use cruise control.

questions.question: Which of these are used on some highways to direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning?

options.text: White lines on the sides of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: White arrows in lanes show you which lanes to use. They tell you whether to go straight or turn.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway is ahead. The road will split into two one-way roads with a median between them. Stay on the right side.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow arrow at a traffic signal?

options.text: Merge into the lane shown by the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
Go ahead. You have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to the lane you came from.
The lane marked with an arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the lane you came from.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you were just in. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow mean at a traffic signal?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a red circle traffic light.
You may turn in the direction the arrow points.
Traffic in that direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a red circle traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red circle light. You must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: It does not matter which lights you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road crosses a divided highway.
You are on a bridge above a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road crosses a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or guide rail.

questions.question: When should you start to speed up after turning?

options.text: Once you are halfway through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Once you are halfway through the turn.
questions.explanation: Begin to speed up near the middle of the turn. Keep looking ahead to where you want to go.

questions.question: If you double your car's speed, by how much does the force of impact increase?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four times.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the greater the force of impact. When you double your speed, the force of impact increases by four times.

questions.question: When may you park or stop on the shoulder of a freeway?

options.text: As long as you turn on your emergency flashers.
If your vehicle is not on the road.
If you need to look at a map.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except when there is an emergency.

questions.question: What does the "P" stand for in the SIPDE acronym?
questions.correctAnswerText: Predict hazards.
questions.explanation: The "P" in SIPDE stands for "Predict hazards." Think about what could go wrong while you are driving and plan what you would do to stay safe.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph needs up to ____ to stop completely.
questions.correctAnswerText: 400 feet
questions.explanation: Tractor-trailers need longer distances to stop than smaller cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer may need almost 400 feet to stop when traveling at 55 mph.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Start signaling as you move into the next lane.
Signal 500 feet before changing lanes on residential streets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Other cars and motorcycles hide in your blind spot. Look over your shoulder before changing lanes. Signal 100 feet before changing lanes on residential streets. Signal 5 seconds before changing lanes on a freeway.

questions.question: When you cannot see well while driving, your first action should be to:

options.text: Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slowing down is your first response when visibility is reduced or road conditions are dangerous.

questions.question: You cannot park within ____ of a fire hydrant.
questions.correctAnswerText: 15 feet
questions.explanation: In Louisiana, you cannot park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

questions.question: You must yield to other drivers:

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When they are on a road to your left and you reach an unmarked intersection at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: When you drive faster, your field of vision:

options.text: Makes it easier to see cross traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gets narrower.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the narrower your field of vision becomes. As speed increases, watch carefully for hazards.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, start by:

options.text: Taking your foot off the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: First, take your foot off the gas pedal. If you need to slow down more, gently and slowly press the brake pedal.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Road changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails ahead and to the right.
Hotel ahead and to the right.
Hospital ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a hospital with emergency services is to the right.

questions.question: At a stop sign, after you stop, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars behind you.
Move when the car ahead moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because vehicles from the left are closer to you. Then look right. Finally, look left again to check for any vehicles you may have missed.

questions.question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes to the left, glance:
questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder.
questions.explanation: Glance over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot.
